newsitem.title: USA: Drug firms see $18.9 bln global R&D spending in 97.
newsitem.headline: Drug firms see $18.9 bln global R&D spending in 97.

text.p: Research-based pharmaceutical companies expect to invest a record $18.9 billion worldwide in research and development in 1997, an 11.5-percent increase from 1996, the industry's main trade group said Wednesday.
The Pharmaceutical Research and Manufacturing of America (PhRMA) said its survey of members showed that about $15 billion of that money will be invested in the United States.
The drug industry said a record 53 medicines were approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration last year.

The group, which has been a sharp critic of the FDA, praised the goverment regulatory agency for speeding up approval, but called for improvements in streamlining the entire multi-year clinical trial and research review that precedes the final drug approval process.

The industry also wants swift renewal of the Prescription Drug User Fee Act of 1992, under which the drug companies pay fees that have helped the FDA get the staff needed to clean up a backlog and streamline approvals.
